issue_context.title: DOCKER-USER table is not created
issue_context.body:
### Description

DOCKER-USER table is not created when ip6tables support is enabled.

### Reproduce

```
/etc/docker/daemon.json
{
    "experimental": true,
    "ip6tables": true
}
```
systemctl start docker

### Expected behavior

DOCKER-USER chain is created.

```
Chain FORWARD (policy DROP 1 packets, 72 bytes)
 pkts bytes target     prot opt in     out     source               destination
 4143 2270K DOCKER-USER  all      *      *       ::/0                 ::/0

Chain DOCKER-USER (1 references)
 pkts bytes target     prot opt in     out     source               destination
 4143 2270K RETURN     all      *      *       ::/0                 ::/0
```

review_comments: At first I was going to comment on the egregious layering violation. Then I saw the implementation of `(*controller).iptablesEnabled`  immediately above. Sigh, libnetwork is the 💩 that keeps on giving.

> At first I was going to comment on the egregious layering violation.

Could you expand a bit more on that?

`c.cfg.DriverCfg["bridge"]` is configuration for the `bridge` network driver. The controller is a layer above drivers and so should not have specific knowledge of how _any_ network driver is configured.
Ah, didn't pay attention to the overall design when doing it. Now I see your point, thanks.
